title_or_table: American Community Survey 1-year estimates, Table B28002, Presence and Types of Internet Subscriptions in Household
table_id: ACS 2025 1-year, B28002 (lines 001, 004 and 007); percent margins from Subject Table S2801 (lines S2801_C02_014 and S2801_C02_017)
geography: 50 states and DC, with a United States row (code US) to set apart; Puerto Rico left out, though the Bureau publishes B28002 and S2801 for it (state 72, read November 13, 2026)
unit: households, with 90 percent margins of error; percentages computed by the studio and stored to four decimals; households_moe is the published margin of the households total (B28002_001M); broadband_any_pct_moe_s2801 and broadband_fixed_pct_moe_s2801 are the shares’ 90 percent margins in percentage points as the Bureau publishes them in S2801, to one decimal; broadband_fixed_pct_moe_formula is the studio’s check by the Bureau’s formula for a proportion
qualification: "Broadband of any type" (line 004) counts a household with a cellular data plan alone; "broadband such as cable, fiber optic or DSL" (line 007) counts fixed service. A chart prints the margins the Bureau publishes in subject table S2801 (broadband_any_pct_moe_s2801, broadband_fixed_pct_moe_s2801). broadband_any_pct_moe, the count’s margin over all households, and broadband_fixed_pct_moe_formula, the Bureau’s formula for a proportion, are the studio’s checks and print nowhere (data lead ruling RF-11a). Compare states only where intervals do not overlap.

domain_note: V7 I015, "Public information is out of reach for some residents", names slow or missing internet service
notes: Margins of the shares (access review S8, D3-905; data lead rulings RF-11 and RF-11a), November 12, 2026. Table B28002 publishes counts and their margins only. The same ACS 2025 1-year release publishes both shares with their margins in Subject Table S2801 (S2801_C02_014 and S2801_C02_017, read from its API; the fixed share’s margins run 0.1 to 1.9 points), and a chart prints those. Every S2801 share equals this file’s share rounded to one decimal, and S2801’s count columns equal B28002’s in all 52 rows. households_moe is B28002_001M, read from the same API call that returned every count and count margin in this file unchanged. broadband_fixed_pct_moe_formula follows formula (6) for a proportion in the Census Bureau’s "Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data: What All Data Users Need to Know" (2020), chapter 8, with its ratio form only where the term under the root is negative; it runs up to 0.25 points from S2801’s (Wyoming, 1.65 against 1.9). Tested against the nation by the gap’s margin with S2801’s margins, 20 states and DC sit above the nation, 22 states below and 8 within; Nevada sits near the line, above it by under 0.02 point (a gap of 0.82 against a margin of 0.81), and moves from within to above when S2801’s margins replace the formula’s (RF-11a).
